title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1LB_1RD1LD_1RE0RA_---0LB_0LF0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1LB_1RD1LD_1RE0RA_---0LB_0LF0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. In each epoch two blocks at the left end grow by eating the tape in front of them (both phases proved in Lean); the rule that sets up the next epoch is not known, and a halt can only happen at the right end, where a short block counts down slowly across epochs.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 55,171 cells have been visited and 35,148 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: At 109 steps: (100)^3733 10 A>1 (011)^6248 (1011)^5940 (10)^2 (1110)^343 (1101)^17 110 (0111)^4 01; at 108: (100)^2044 10 D>0 111 (011)^1277 (1011)^1830 (1110)^25 (0111)^19 (1011)^4 101. The exponents decrease to the right, as in a counter whose inner digits tick over only when the outer ones finish.

claims.title: The two growth phases
claims.text: Y n p R = 0^inf D> 0111011 (011)^n (1011)^p R: Y n p (1111 R) reaches Y (n+1) (p+1) R in 10n+10p+35 steps, and Y n p ((1110)^(k+2) 1 R) reaches Y (n+2) (p+1) ((1110)^(k+1) 1 R) in 20n+20p+86 steps, for all n, p, k and every tape R; both iterated.

claims.title: Epochs and a slow counter at the right end
claims.text: The run is a sequence of epochs; each starts from a short left part and a middle (1011 10)^K (1011)^X (K = 24, 75, 102, 395, 223, 1685, 1264 at the main starts up to 1.7·10<sup>8</sup> steps), and a short block (1110)^k at the right end counts down slowly across epochs (20, 19, 18, 17).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Missing: the epoch map and the behaviour of the slow counter at the right end; see Next steps in the README.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 55,171 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two blocks that grow by eating the tape in front of them
html: Look at the tape each time the head comes back to the left end in state D. It starts with two blocks, (011)^n and (1011)^p, and both keep growing:
They grow by eating what lies in front of them, in two phases, each proved in Lean for blocks of any size:

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 100' role='img' aria-label='two growing blocks eat the run in front of them' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><rect x='10' y='15' width='140' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='80' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(011)^n</text><rect x='150' y='15' width='120' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='210' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(1011)^p</text><rect x='270' y='15' width='200' height='22' fill='none' stroke='var(--head)'/><text x='370' y='30' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>food: 1111 1111 ...</text><rect x='10' y='60' width='160' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='90' y='75' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(011)^(n+1)</text><rect x='170' y='60' width='140' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='240' y='75' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>(1011)^(p+1)</text><rect x='310' y='60' width='160' height='22' fill='none' stroke='var(--head)'/><text x='390' y='75' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--fg2)'>1111 ...</text></svg>

When the food runs out, the tape is reorganized and a new epoch starts, with a new long stretch of food. The sizes at the epoch starts are irregular (24, 75, 102, 395, 223, 1685, 1264 units), and the rule that produces them is not known yet. Meanwhile a short block at the far right end counts down very slowly from one epoch to the next (20, 19, 18, 17, ...).

Where it could halt

Only at the right end of the tape: in state E reading a blank cell next to a particular pattern. That is where the slow counter lives, so a halt would come when that structure runs out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 55,171 cells (44,694 left of the start, 39 right), with a density of 1s of 0.637.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Epochs in which two blocks (011)^n (1011)^p at the left end grow by eating the tape in front of them in two proved phases, while a short block at the right end counts down slowly; the epoch rule is unknown; open.
family: growing blocks with epochs and a slow counter
